method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); one module of exported questions with the s 14ZZW prohibition as a regulative rule run by EVALTRACE inside a question that takes only plain facts, one case file; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate. Added beside baseline-2026-10 and naive-2026-10, which are untouched.

seat: the individual who discloses, or may disclose, information about an entity's tax affairs (the eligible whistleblower, or anyone disclosing to a lawyer, doctor or psychologist), and who brings or may bring a claim for detriment or threats suffered because of it (taa-whistleblower.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run taa-whistleblower.l4 ; l4 run taa-whistleblower-cases.l4
checks.result: 114 assertions written, 114 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read; two deliberately wrong assertions on the trace helper were run once in a scratch file (since deleted) and showed as DiagnosticSeverity_Error, assertion failed. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: Focus: Part IVD, protection for tax whistleblowers, the provisions a claimant meets. In: s 2 (eligible recipient, eligible whistleblower), ss 14ZZT, 14ZZU, 14ZZV, 14ZZW, 14ZZX, 14ZZXA, 14ZZY, 14ZZZ, 14ZZZAA, 14ZZZA, 14ZZZB, 14ZZZC, 14ZZZD; Regulations ss 13A, 13B. Out: s 14ZZTA (information-handling machinery), s 14ZZZE (Commonwealth compensation for acquisition of property), application and transitional provisions, Schedule 1 Division 355, Crimes Act 1914 s 4B(3), the Criminal Code's fault elements and defences (asked as facts). Reasons in NOTES.md.
